name: The Content Engine: 12 Prompts for Solo Founders
tagline: Turn a single core business idea into a full week of high-converting social media posts in minutes.
metaDescription: Transform one business idea into a full week of engaging posts. 12 plug-and-play AI prompts designed specifically for solo founders and indie makers.
description:
# The Content Engine

Running a solo business leaves very few hours in the day for marketing. If you are tired of staring at a blank screen trying to figure out what to tweet, post, or publish, this toolkit is for you.

### Who It Is For
This digital product is built exclusively for bootstrapped founders, indie hackers, and solo creators who need to build in public and drive inbound leads without hiring an agency.

### The Problem It Solves
Most founders struggle with consistency because they treat every post as a brand-new creative challenge. This leads to burnout and erratic publishing schedules.

### Why These Prompts Work
Instead of asking generic AI tools to "write a post," these prompts use constrained frameworks based on high-performing copywriting models. They force the LLM to extract nuances from your single core idea—such as customer pain points, counterintuitive opinions, and behind-the-scenes metrics—and expand them into platform-native formats. 

Each prompt includes specific usage tips to ensure your brand voice remains authentic, punchy, and human.
includes: 12 detailed usage tips for solo founders
Compatible with ChatGPT, Claude, and local LLMs
sampleItems: Write a contrarian thread starter about [Core Idea] that challenges conventional wisdom in the [Industry] space, using a 4-part hook structure.
Draft a milestone update about [Core Idea] focusing on the hard lessons learned rather than just the vanity metrics.

items.title: The Contrarian Take
items.body: Act as an expert copywriter in the [Industry] niche. Write a 3-part hook and opening paragraph for a social media post that challenges the most common piece of advice regarding [Core Idea]. Make it provocative yet defensible. Contrast what people usually do with the smarter, counterintuitive approach you took. Avoid buzzwords like 'synergy' or 'game-changer'. Keep the tone direct, conversational, and authoritative, ending with an open question that invites debate from peers in your space.

items.title: The Behind-The-Scenes Breakdown
items.body: Act as a transparent startup founder sharing a raw update. Take the concept of [Core Idea] and break it down into an unvarnished diary entry for social media. Detail one specific mistake made, one unexpected realization, and one tactical takeaway that other solo founders can apply to their own projects today. Write in the first person, use short punchy sentences, and omit any corporate fluff. The goal is to build deep trust through radical honesty.

items.title: The Customer Pain Point Agitator
items.body: Act as a direct-response marketer. Write a short-form post targeting solo founders who are struggling with [Core Idea]. Start by vividly describing the frustrating daily reality of dealing with this problem. Pivot quickly to introduce your perspective or product as the logical relief valve. Use a clear before-and-after contrast. Conclude with a low-friction call to action directing readers to check out your primary offering in the replies.

items.title: The Step-by-Step Playbook
items.body: Act as a technical educator. Convert [Core Idea] into a concise, 5-step actionable framework that a busy founder can implement in under an hour. Use clear numbered lists, action verbs for each step, and include a brief 'pro tip' or common pitfall to avoid for step number three. The formatting must be clean and easily scannable for mobile readers scrolling quickly through their feeds.

items.title: The Milestone & Metrics Share
items.body: Act as a data-driven indie hacker. Frame a recent update regarding [Core Idea] around a specific data point, revenue number, or user growth metric. Explain the context behind the number without sounding boastful. Highlight the exact experiment or change that caused the metric to move. End with an encouragement to other bootstrapped founders who might be stuck at the previous milestone.

items.title: The Founder's Manifesto
items.body: Act as a visionary early-stage founder. Write a philosophical post exploring why [Core Idea] matters deeply to the future of the [Industry] market. Focus on your core beliefs, why you decided to build a solo business around this thesis, and what you hope to change. Use an inspiring, reflective tone with rhythmic sentence structures that read almost like poetry.

items.title: The FAQ Myth-Buster
items.body: Act as a customer support lead turned educator. Take the single most frequent objection or misconception about [Core Idea] that you hear from potential users. Write a post that directly addresses the myth, explains why people fall for it, and presents clear evidence refuting it. Maintain a helpful, patient, yet confident tone throughout.

items.title: The Quick Win Checklist
items.body: Act as a productivity coach for creators. Design a rapid-fire checklist centered around [Core Idea] that can be executed on a Friday afternoon. Use checkbox emojis and keep each item under ten words. Add a closing line telling readers to comment 'CHECK' if they want a deeper dive into item number two.

items.title: The Prediction Post
items.body: Act as an industry analyst looking ahead over the next 12 months. Make three bold predictions about how [Core Idea] will evolve within the [Industry] landscape. Support each prediction with one micro-trend you are currently observing in your own solo business operations. Keep the outlook realistic yet forward-thinking.

items.title: The Failure Autopsy
items.body: Act as a reflective entrepreneur. Share a specific failure or failed experiment related to [Core Idea]. Walk the reader through your hypothesis, what went wrong, how much time or money it cost, and the exact rule you created for your business as a result. Emphasize the psychological aspect of bouncing back as a solo operator.

items.title: The Resource Roundup
items.body: Act as a generous curator in the [Industry] ecosystem. List three underrated tools, templates, or mental models that help you execute [Core Idea] more efficiently. Provide a one-sentence description of why you use each item personally. Do not include affiliate links; focus entirely on pure, high-value recommendations to build community goodwill.

items.title: The Direct Pitch
items.body: Act as a high-converting copywriter. Write a crisp, benefit-driven promotional post for your product or service tied directly to [Core Idea]. Highlight the primary transformation, address the cost of inaction, and provide a clear, frictionless call to action with a link. Keep the entire text under 150 words for maximum impact on fast-moving feeds.
